title: Present perfect with for / since + possessives + Saxon genitive
title_it: Present perfect con for e since, possessivi e genitivo sassone
goal: Say how long a situation has lasted with for, since and how long, use possessive adjectives and pronouns, and use the Saxon genitive.
goal_it: Dire da quanto tempo dura una situazione con for, since e how long, usare aggettivi e pronomi possessivi e il genitivo sassone.

steps.title: Present perfect with for and since
steps.title_it: Present perfect con for e since
en: We use the present perfect to say how long a situation has lasted up to now. It started in the past and it is still true: I have lived in Leeds for two years (and I still live there).

for + a period of time: for two hours, for three days, for ten years. since + the moment when it started: since Monday, since 2019, since I was ten. The question is How long have you lived here? (never 'how long time').

Some verbs are not used in the continuous form (be, know, have, like, want, understand). With them we use the present perfect simple: I have known him for ten years. I have had this phone since March.
it: Usiamo il present perfect per dire da quanto tempo dura una situazione fino a ora. E' iniziata nel passato ed e' ancora vera: I have lived in Leeds for two years (e ci vivo ancora).

for + un periodo di tempo (per, da): for two hours, for three days, for ten years. since + il momento in cui e' iniziata (da): since Monday, since 2019, since I was ten. La domanda e' How long have you lived here? (mai 'how long time').

Alcuni verbi non si usano nella forma continua (be, know, have, like, want, understand). Con questi si usa il present perfect simple: I have known him for ten years. I have had this phone since March. Attenzione: in italiano diciamo 'vivo qui da due anni' (presente), ma in inglese NON si dice 'I live here for two years'.

examples.en: I have waited for the bus for twenty minutes.
She has worked here since January.
We have known them for years.
How long have you had your car?
examples.it: Da quanto tempo hai la macchina?

steps.title: Negatives, questions and past or present perfect?
steps.title_it: Negative, domande e past simple o present perfect?
en: Negative: I haven't eaten for two days. She hasn't called me since Monday. In the negative we use the simple form (haven't eaten), not the continuous.
Questions: How long have you known her? How long has he worked here? Short answers: For two years. / Since 2022.

Compare the two tenses. I lived in Rome for two years = it is finished, I do not live there now. I have lived in Rome for two years = I still live there. With a finished period (from 2018 to 2020, last year) we use the past simple.
it: Negativa: I haven't eaten for two days. She hasn't called me since Monday. Nella negativa si usa la forma semplice (haven't eaten), non quella continua.
Domande: How long have you known her? How long has he worked here? Risposte brevi: For two years. / Since 2022.

Confronta i due tempi. I lived in Rome for two years = e' finito, non vivo piu' li'. I have lived in Rome for two years = ci vivo ancora. Con un periodo finito (from 2018 to 2020, last year) si usa il past simple. Giovedi' vedrai anche la forma continua (have been living).

head: Sentence
What it means
rows: I lived in Rome for two years.
I do not live in Rome now.
I have lived in Rome for two years.
I haven't seen Tom since May.
The last time was in May.
How long have you been here?

examples.en: He hasn't phoned me for a week.
examples.it: Non mi telefona da una settimana.

examples.en: They lived in Wales from 2015 to 2019.
examples.it: Hanno vissuto in Galles dal 2015 al 2019.

examples.en: How long has she had that bag?
examples.it: Da quanto tempo ha quella borsa?

steps.title: Possessive adjectives and pronouns
en: A possessive adjective goes before a noun: my car, your keys, her sister. We never use the with it: the my car is wrong. A possessive pronoun stands alone and replaces the noun: This is my phone and that one is yours.
Its has no pronoun. Remember: it's means it is (it's late); its means 'of it' (the cat licked its paw).
it: L'aggettivo possessivo sta davanti a un nome: my car, your keys, her sister. Non si mette mai the: the my car e' sbagliato. Il pronome possessivo sta da solo e sostituisce il nome: This is my phone and that one is yours.
Its non ha il pronome. Ricorda: it's significa it is (it's late); its significa 'suo' (the cat licked its paw).

examples.en: Our flat is smaller than theirs.
examples.it: Il nostro appartamento e' piu' piccolo del loro.

examples.en: Is this your umbrella? No, mine is red.
examples.it: E' tuo questo ombrello? No, il mio e' rosso.

examples.en: I left my coat there and she left hers here.
examples.it: Io ho lasciato il mio cappotto li' e lei ha lasciato il suo qui.

steps.title: The Saxon genitive: 's
en: For people and animals we add 's to the owner and the owner comes FIRST: Carlo's car (the car of Carlo), the dog's tail. It is an Italian mistake to say the car of Carlo.
Plural nouns ending in -s take only an apostrophe: the girls' room. Irregular plurals take 's: the children's toys. With names ending in -s we write James's bike (or James' bike).
For things we usually do not use 's. We say the leg of the table or the table leg, the door of the car or the car door.
Whose is it? Whose coat is this? It's Anna's. (Anna's = Anna's coat).
it: Per persone e animali si aggiunge 's al possessore e il possessore viene PRIMA: Carlo's car (la macchina di Carlo), the dog's tail. E' un errore italiano dire the car of Carlo.
I plurali in -s prendono solo l'apostrofo: the girls' room. I plurali irregolari prendono 's: the children's toys. Con i nomi in -s si scrive James's bike (o James' bike).
Per le cose di solito non si usa 's. Si dice the leg of the table oppure the table leg, the door of the car oppure the car door.
Whose is it? Whose coat is this? It's Anna's. (Anna's = il cappotto di Anna).

examples.en: My sister's husband is a pilot.
examples.it: Il marito di mia sorella e' un pilota.

examples.en: The dog's bowl is under the table.
examples.it: La ciotola del cane e' sotto il tavolo.

examples.en: That is Maria's bike, not mine.
examples.it: Quella e' la bici di Maria, non la mia.

steps.q: I have lived here ___ 2019.
steps.q_it: Vivo qui ___ il 2019.
steps.why: 2019 is the moment when it started, so we use since.
steps.why_it: 2019 e' il momento in cui e' iniziato: si usa since.

steps.q: He has been in Italy ___ three weeks.
steps.q_it: E' in Italia da tre settimane.
steps.why: Three weeks is a period of time: for.
steps.why_it: Tre settimane e' un periodo di tempo: for.

steps.q: I ___ (know) Sara for ten years.
steps.q_it: Conosco Sara da dieci anni.
steps.why: Know is a state verb: present perfect simple, with for + a period.
steps.why_it: Know e' un verbo di stato: present perfect simple, con for + un periodo.

steps.q: Marta has lived in Leeds for two years. What does this tell us?
steps.q_it: Marta has lived in Leeds for two years. Cosa ci dice?
options: She lived in Leeds, but she has moved away
She is going to live in Leeds for two years
She has never lived in Leeds
steps.why: The present perfect with for means the situation continues until now.
steps.why_it: Il present perfect con for significa che la situazione continua fino a ora.

steps.q: ___ have you had this phone?
steps.q_it: Da quanto tempo hai questo telefono?
steps.why: How long asks about duration: How long have you had...?
steps.why_it: How long chiede la durata: How long have you had...?

steps.q: Order the words: a question about duration.
steps.q_it: Riordina: una domanda sulla durata.
answers: How long have you lived in this flat?
steps.why: How long + have + subject + past participle.
steps.why_it: How long + have + soggetto + participio passato.

steps.q: I ___ (have) this bike since 2020.
steps.q_it: Ho questa bici dal 2020.
steps.why: Have (own) is a state verb: I have had. Since 2020 = starting point.
steps.why_it: Have (possesso) e' un verbo di stato: I have had. Since 2020 = momento iniziale.

steps.q: I ___ in Madrid for three years, but now I live in Lisbon.
steps.q_it: Ho vissuto a Madrid per tre anni, ma ora vivo a Lisbona.
steps.why: The period in Madrid is finished: past simple. Have lived would mean I still live there.
steps.why_it: Il periodo a Madrid e' finito: past simple. Have lived significherebbe che ci vivo ancora.

steps.q: She hasn't called me ___ Monday.
steps.q_it: Non mi chiama da lunedi'.
steps.why: Monday is a starting point: since.
steps.why_it: Lunedi' e' un punto di partenza: since.

steps.q: Is this pen yours? No, ___ is in my bag.
steps.q_it: E' tua questa penna? No, la mia e' nella borsa.
steps.why: There is no noun after the gap, so we need the pronoun: mine.
steps.why_it: Dopo lo spazio non c'e' un nome: serve il pronome mine.

steps.q: Sara and Tom love ___ new flat.
steps.q_it: Sara e Tom adorano il loro nuovo appartamento.
steps.why: Before a noun we use the adjective: their.
steps.why_it: Davanti a un nome si usa l'aggettivo: their.

steps.q: I left my bag at home. Can I use ___? (you)
steps.q_it: Ho lasciato la borsa a casa. Posso usare la tua?
steps.why: Alone, without a noun: yours.
steps.why_it: Da solo, senza nome: yours.

steps.q: The dog is hungry. ___ bowl is empty.
steps.q_it: Il cane ha fame. La sua ciotola e' vuota.
steps.why: Possessive adjective of it: its (no apostrophe).
steps.why_it: Aggettivo possessivo di it: its (senza apostrofo).

steps.q: Which sentence is correct?
steps.q_it: Quale frase e' corretta?
options: The my sister is a doctor.
steps.why: Adjective my before the noun, with no article.
steps.why_it: Aggettivo my davanti al nome, senza articolo.

steps.q: This is the car of Carlo. = This is ___ car.
steps.q_it: Questa e' la macchina di Carlo.
steps.why: Owner first + 's: Carlo's car.
steps.why_it: Prima il possessore + 's: Carlo's car.

steps.q: Two girls share a room. How do we say 'la stanza delle ragazze'?
steps.q_it: Due ragazze dividono una stanza. Come si dice 'la stanza delle ragazze'?
steps.why: A plural noun in -s takes only the apostrophe: the girls' room.
steps.why_it: Un plurale in -s prende solo l'apostrofo: the girls' room.

steps.q: Order the words.
steps.q_it: Riordina.
steps.why: Possessive adjective + genitive + adjective + noun.
steps.why_it: Aggettivo possessivo + genitivo + aggettivo + nome.

steps.q: Which sentence is correct?
steps.q_it: Quale frase e' corretta?
options: The my father's car is old.
Car of my father is old.
steps.why: The owner comes first with 's, and no the before my.
steps.why_it: Il possessore viene prima con 's e non si mette the davanti a my.

steps.q: Order the words.
steps.q_it: Riordina.
steps.why: Whose + noun + is + this.
steps.why_it: Whose + nome + is + this.

steps.q: This is not my phone. It's ___ (Anna).
steps.q_it: Questo non e' il mio telefono. E' di Anna.
steps.why: Anna's phone, without repeating the noun.
steps.why_it: Il telefono di Anna, senza ripetere il nome.

steps.q: Review. Right now we ___ for the bus.
steps.q_it: Ripasso. In questo momento stiamo aspettando l'autobus.
steps.why: Right now: present continuous.
steps.why_it: Right now: present continuous.

steps.q: Review. My brother usually ___ (walk) to work, but today he is taking the bus.
steps.q_it: Ripasso. Mio fratello di solito va a piedi al lavoro, ma oggi prende l'autobus.
steps.why: Usually: habit, present simple, he + -s.
steps.why_it: Usually: abitudine, present simple, he + -s.

steps.q: Review. Last night we ___ a film when the power went off.
steps.q_it: Ripasso. Ieri sera guardavamo un film quando e' saltata la corrente.
steps.why: The film was in progress when the power went off: past continuous.
steps.why_it: Il film era in corso quando e' saltata la corrente: past continuous.

steps.q: Review. We ___ (not / go) to the cinema last Saturday.
steps.q_it: Ripasso. Lo scorso sabato non siamo andati al cinema.
steps.why: Last Saturday is finished: past simple, did + not + base verb.
steps.why_it: Last Saturday e' finito: past simple, did + not + verbo base.

steps.q: Review. Have you ever ___ a horse?
steps.q_it: Ripasso. Hai mai cavalcato un cavallo?
steps.why: Have + past participle: ridden.
steps.why_it: Have + participio passato: ridden.

steps.q: Review. Order the words.
steps.q_it: Ripasso. Riordina.
answers: I have never been to Spain.
steps.why: Never goes between have and the participle.
steps.why_it: Never va tra have e il participio.

How long have you known him?

cards.ex: I have known her for ten years.
This pen is mine, that one is yours.

cards.it: il suo / il nostro / il loro
cards.ex: The red car is ours, the blue one is theirs.
